text.p: Following are the main stories in Thursday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Unskilled male foreign workers with six-month work permits are not allowed to marry Malaysian women with immediate effect, and will be deported with their wives if found to do so, said Deputy Home Minister Megat Junid Megat Ayob.
-- Candidates for next month's UMNO elections are not allowed to give interviews on political matters to the media, Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said.

-- Measat Broadcast Network Systems expects its digital satellite television and radio network launched on Wednesday to break even in three years with subscriber base of 700,000, said its chief operating officer Paul Edwards.
-- A list of the first 20 to 30 counters permitted to be traded under regulated short-selling will be released on Friday, a Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange official said.

-- Property concern Island & Peninsular expects to embark on two township projects in the north next year at an estimated total cost of 1.2 billion ringgit, group managing director Mohd Yusof Hussin said in an interview.
